body: true-up-rewrites-uncommitted-suite-edit: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:materialize_steps (line 4016) adds 'stale: <path> differs from the carried v<version> rendering' and queues the rewrite whenever read_text(path) != body, with no call to uncommitted(); the git-state check uncommitted() (line 570) is used only by removal_split (line 609) and the archive steps, so a removal of a suite file with an uncommitted change archives it, while a rewrite of a stamped file with the same change does not. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: a stamped suite file that a person appends to still carries its stamp, so true-up-asks-once-before-destructive-steps does not count its rewrite as destructive ('rewrites a file a person edited, which is every file but a suite-owned file that still carries its stamp or its fixed content'), the plan holds no destructive step, and /ok runs it with no question; the edit lands in no archive and, uncommitted, in no commit. Corpus: story:true-up-project-estate promises 'so that upgrading the suite never costs me work I wrote'. decision:whole-file-ownership says 'True-up rewrites a suite-owned file that carries its stamp or its fixed content with no question' and limits 'so true-up never discards uncommitted work' to 'any other file true-up would remove'. decision:true-up-asks-once-before-destructive-steps defines destructive as above. decision:retired-layout-strips-only-recoverable-files bears on recoverability. The story and the decisions cannot both hold for this file, so the owner chooses. Harm: A1/A2-weight loss of uncommitted owner text; the fix changes corpus commitments either way. Options: A. whole-file-ownership and true-up-asks-once count a rewrite of a stamped suite file with an uncommitted or staged-only change as destructive: true-up archives the working copy first and the plan asks; cost: a question on upgrades where the owner hand-edited a file whose stamp says do not hand-edit, and a new git-state check on every stale step. B. whole-file-ownership states that a stamped file's uncommitted edits are discarded on rewrite, and true-up-project-estate narrows 'work I wrote' to files the owner owns; cost: an owner who edits a stamped file loses the edit with no notice. C. true-up rewrites with no question but archives the uncommitted working copy and names it in its report, with no consent step; cost: the archive grows with a copy the owner may not want, and whole-file-ownership must say a rewrite can archive without consent, departing from 'moves a file into the archive' being destructive. D. true-up rewrites with no question and only names each discarded uncommitted change by path in its report; cost: the edit is still lost, only named. No stated rule decides among them. Siblings: none open.

The story's realizing sites are scripts/tasks:calls_table (line 1297) and the calls rows in skills/converge/SKILL.md:The return and plan-sprint/sprint-document.md step 13, all payload. Mechanism: the sprint build rule (sprint-document.md step 8: 'every new or amended story implemented in code carries the @story: annotation at the site that realizes it') and the standalone check leave no compliant site for a story realized only in payload. Corpus: concept:annotation, 'Each annotation marks a load-bearing site'; decision:code-cites-design, 'Every annotation resolves to a live artifact of the named kind' and 'whoever consults an artifact while working on a file leaves the annotation'; concept:citation-tag, tags are 'owner-declared configuration of the suite's lint'. decision:whole-file-ownership and concept:materialized-artifact are silent on stripping. The change is to the project's own tooling: checks/materialized-standalone, admin/true-up's materialization, and the build rule in plan-sprint/sprint-document.md step 8 or the build prompt in skills/_sprint/shared.md. No accept-list harm: a missing annotation is navigation only. Options: A. materialized-standalone accepts a design citation in a payload script where it resolves here, and true-up strips citation lines when it materializes, so consumers see none; scripts/tasks:calls_table carries the annotation; cost: a second transform in materialization, and the vendored copy differs from the source by those lines. B. materialized-standalone accepts the citation and true-up copies it as written; cost: a consumer's lint flags a tag it has not declared, or resolves it against a consumer corpus that lacks the slug. C. payload files carry no annotations, and the build rule and the project rules say so; a story realized only in payload is cited from a repository-only site (a check under checks/) or not at all; cost: the annotation grep does not find the realizing code. No stated rule decides among them. Siblings: plain-converge-return-offers-no-veto (same story).

Options: A. the story is met in a plain run by the shown table plus the intake, which any person files into, and the return keeps asking nothing; cost: the owner turns a disagreement into an issue by hand, and an overturn has no path that names the call's row. B. a plain run's return asks which calls-table rows the owner vetoes and files one issue per vetoed row, as sprint mode's step 13 does; cost: an unattended run ends with a question, against 'it asks the owner nothing'. C. the return asks nothing, and the archive-and-commit offer, which already waits for the owner, also takes vetoes in the same answer; cost: one answer carries two acts, and a veto after the commit still needs a hand-filed issue. body: certification-fix-leaves-documentation: Judgment issue (it carries a Stuck in converge-2026-10-17T021110 section), so route question. Evidence, re-verified at the tree as staged: the harm stands. The kept fix i72 widened the prose scope rule: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_converge/coding-rules.md:38-62 ({{PROSE-SCOPE-RULE}}) now puts in review documentation under a docspec whose ## References 'that sprint's change, its certification fixes included, reaches', and converge/SKILL.md:40 restates it. The backed-out fix i73 left the fixer and verifier unchanged: converge/prompts/fix.md:24 still reads 'Change nothing the defect does not need: no rename, no reshaping, no fix of something you happened to notice.', and fix.md has no step that reads a docspec; converge/prompts/verify.md:9 still reads 'You check the change, and only the change'. The review root (converge/SKILL.md:101) runs its documentation passes once, before any fix. So documentation is in review after a certification fix, but no agent reads it after the fix. Mechanism: (1) a certification fix that changes an observable behavior lands in the sprint's commit with the documentation describing the old behavior; (2) the next /plan-sprint reconcile window starts after that commit (decision closing-commit-baseline), so nothing flags it. Corpus: story keep-documentation-current, 'each change to my product bring the documentation it affects along in the same change, so that the documentation a reader finds at any commit describes the product at that commit'; decision sprints-write-the-documentation, 'Sprint certification reviews each touched documentation against its docspec and the change' and 'Outside these, documentation stays as it is' (silent on certification fixes); concept docspec, 'A docspec lets a change find the documentation it affects'. The two reach paths are stated at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md:173 (a reference, or a file the surface intent names as declaring a listed class) and the C5 omission check at converge/prompts/sprint-pass.md:28 ('Report each public element the documentation omits'). Harm: A3 as filed (/converge sprint gives a wrong result); the story is the commitment, so this is the owner's choice of mechanism after two fixes stuck. Options: (Tried 1) fixer step 4 plus verifier step 4 over code-path references only; the verifier sent it back for converge/SKILL.md:40 restating the old rule, then fix 2 fixed that, and the confirm driver sent it back: the listed-class reach path of artifact-definitions.md:173 is missed, and a fix that adds a public element makes no sentence false, so ## Lists or ## Covers omissions go unchecked; backed out. (A, untried) fixer and verifier bring along documentation by both reach paths, editing false sentences and adding each public element the fix added; cost: every certification fix reads the surface intent and docspec index. (B, untried) re-run the documentation pass of each docspec a fix reached after the fix loop, its C5 findings joining a further fix round; cost: one pass per reached docspec and a longer loop, reusing sprint-pass.md:28's existing check, so one check rather than a second copy in fix.md and verify.md. (C) certification fixes leave documentation alone and the completion report lists each docspec a fix reached for the next sprint; cost: the sprint commit lands stale, against the story's 'at any commit', so C needs a story delta. Siblings to rule together: converge-commits-leave-documentation-behind (same story, plain runs), listed-class-change-reach (how a declaring-file change reaches a docspec, the gap that sent fix 2 back), out-of-band-review-misses-declaring-files.

converge-commits-leave-documentation-behind: route question: two live commitments cannot both hold for a plain /converge run's commits. Evidence, re-verified: the filed facts hold. The prose scope rule at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_converge/coding-rules.md:59-61 still reads 'Anywhere else, and in a run that certifies no sprint, file no finding on it and edit none of it.' A drive, analysis, or defects run fixes product code and ends with an offer to commit (converge SKILL description), so a fix that changes behavior a docspec references is committed with that documentation stale. Mechanism: the documentation catches up only at the next /plan-sprint, whose reconcile flags 'Code or corpus a docspec references, changed outside a sprint' (decision out-of-band-documentation-reconciled), so between the plain run's commit and the next sprint the documentation describes the old behavior. Corpus: story keep-documentation-current, 'each change to my product bring the documentation it affects along in the same change, so that the documentation a reader finds at any commit describes the product at that commit'; decision sprints-write-the-documentation, 'Of the suite's runs, only a sprint writes a project's documentation; a person's edit outside a sprint is reconciled at planning' and 'Outside these, documentation stays as it is'; decision out-of-band-documentation-reconciled already gives the catch-up path for code changed outside a sprint. The fix is a corpus change either way, so no run could make it (left alone in converge-2026-10-17T021110). Options: (A) the decision admits a /converge fix bringing along the documentation its change reaches, with the prose scope rule and fix and verify prompts widened to match; cost: plain runs read docspecs and the surface intent and edit documentation, which shares the mechanism question of certification-fix-leaves-documentation. (B) the story scopes 'at any commit' to the commits a sprint makes, and plain-run commits wait for the next reconcile, which decision out-of-band-documentation-reconciled already performs; cost: documentation is stale between a plain run and the next sprint, and the story's promise narrows. (C, the filer missed it) a plain run brings no documentation along but files, through the owner list, a judgment or defect issue naming each docspec a committed fix reached, so the gap is recorded before the commit rather than found at reconcile; cost: still stale between commits, plus an intake write per reached docspec, and the story still needs B's narrowing. This project declares no docspec yet (no .ok-planner/docspec/; see readme-docspec-and-surface-intent-unwritten), so the harm reaches consumer projects, not this tree today. Siblings to rule together: certification-fix-leaves-documentation, listed-class-change-reach, out-of-band-review-misses-declaring-files.

draft-sprint-indistinguishable-from-approved: route question: the answer either keeps or widens what story plan-a-sprint promises. The template plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md carries no approval field. A grep of converge/SKILL.md, converge/prompts/sprint-review.md, and _tasks/drain.md finds no approval check. SKILL.md:154 already relies on promotions landing only after approval, so the intake is safe; only the sprint file is ambiguous. Corpus: story plan-a-sprint, 'a signed-off, self-sufficient sprint, so that any executor can realize my intent'; concept sprint, 'A sprint owns approved intent'; decision final-form-deltas, 'restricting corpus change to the delta is what gives the ceremony's sign-off its weight'. None says how an executor tells a signed-off sprint from a draft. Harm: an executor pointed at a draft applies deltas the owner never approved, against final-form-deltas. Options: (A) the story owes only a signed-off sprint at the ceremony's end, and a dead session's draft is the owner's to discard; cost: an executor pointed at a draft runs it, and nothing warns. (B) a sprint carries an approval mark that Approval writes, and every executor refuses a sprint without it; cost: a template field, a write at Approval, and a refusal in each executor; sprints already approved before the change lack the mark, so the refusal needs a migration or an exemption for them (release boundary: stored state). (C, the filer missed it) the session drafts under a draft path, such as a -draft suffix, and moves the file and its delta sidecar to its final name at Approval, so only approved sprints carry a sprint name; cost: code planners and reviewers read the draft path, and every reference written during planning moves at Approval; executors need no refusal but an executor given the draft path still runs it. body: listed-class-change-reach: Evidence, re-verified at the working tree: the derived reach the filer describes is built at every site it names. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md:173 (the ## Lists bullet) ends 'A sprint whose work reaches a file the surface intent names as declaring a listed class, or whose surface intent delta changes the rule, an exception, or the declaring line of a listed class, carries a work item that updates the documentation'; :172 keeps '## References ... A sprint whose work reaches a reference carries a work item'. plan-sprint/SKILL.md:105 (The documentation match) adds the same two reach paths beside the reference match; plan-sprint/core.md:38-41 (IMPLEMENTATION-NOTES-FORM Docspecs: line) and :317-319 (CODE-PLANNER-PROMPT step 8) match declaring files; _sprint/shared.md:383-392 (certification reading step 6) does the same. The out-of-band reviewer test at plan-sprint/core.md:121 still names only 'a corpus artifact, or a file under a code path, that a docspec's References names' (sibling out-of-band-review-misses-declaring-files). This repository keeps no .ok-planner/docspec/ or surface intent; the question is about the shipped tooling. Mechanism: the docspec index (.ok-planner/docspec.md) carries each docspec's Where and References only, so under the derived reading every matcher (planning, code planning, certification, the out-of-band reviewer) must also read the docspec's ## Lists and the surface intent's '## Where each class is declared'; under the declared reading a matcher reads the index alone, but a surface intent delta that reclassifies a class, or a declaring file the intent adds later, reaches no docspec unless References names it. Corpus: decision:sprints-write-the-documentation says 'Planning reads the docspecs' index and matches the drafted work against each docspec's references, the corpus artifacts and code paths its documentation describes'; decision:one-docspec-per-file says 'Planning reads the index to match drafted work against every docspec's references'; decision:out-of-band-documentation-reconciled flags 'Code or corpus a docspec references, changed outside a sprint'; concept:docspec says 'Each docspec names what its documentation describes, so whoever plans a change matches the change against those names' and 'a reference docspec names the classes it must list'; decision:surface-members-listed-at-need says the surface intent names the declaring files and members are listed from them at need. story:reference-names-the-public-surface owes a reference that names 'every element I made public and no element I kept internal'; story:keep-documentation-current owes documentation that moves 'in the same change'. The corpus is silent on whether a ## Lists class reaches by itself; its matching sentences name references only, so option A (as built) widens those decisions and needs a delta to sprints-write-the-documentation, one-docspec-per-file, and out-of-band-documentation-reconciled to say a listed class's declaring files and surface-intent changes reach too, while option B fits their words but must add a rule that References names every declaring file of each listed class and the compliance reviewer enforces it. Harm at stake: a reference left stale after a change that adds or reclassifies a public element (the story's promise); no accept-list entry is in play, this is a commitment choice. Options: A. Derived reach, as built; cost: every matcher reads the surface intent and each ## Lists, the index alone no longer answers the match, and three decisions take a delta. B. Declared reach: a reference docspec's ## References must name the declaring files of every class it lists, enforced at review, and matching reads references alone; cost: a surface intent delta that reclassifies a class or adds a declaring file reaches no docspec until a docspec delta follows, so the story can fail silently. C (the filer missed): B, plus a reference docspec with ## Lists names the surface intent file itself among its References, so every surface intent delta reaches it; cost: every intent delta touches every reference docspec, even one changing a class it does not list, and the index still misses a declaring file added later unless the docspec is amended. Rule it with out-of-band-review-misses-declaring-files and lists-section-internal-class-exceptions.

lists-section-internal-class-exceptions: Evidence, re-verified at the working tree: the reading the filer describes is built. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md:173 reads '## Lists ... names one class of public surface per bullet, in the surface intent's terms: a class whose rule makes its members public, or one whose exceptions make a member public ... for a class its rule makes public, every member but those its exceptions make internal; for a class its rule keeps internal, only the members its exceptions make public'. The builder's listing rule at _sprint/shared.md:123-134 (DOCUMENTATION-RULE) follows it, and the C5 row at _sprint/shared.md:315 checks 'a public element of a class its ## Lists names is missing, an element the surface intent keeps internal is listed'. This repository keeps no docspec or surface intent; the question is about the shipped tooling. Mechanism: under the surface intent's form (decision:surface-intent-is-one-prose-document: 'which classes of element are public by default, with the specific elements that depart from those rules named'), a public element can belong to a class whose rule keeps it internal; such an element reaches a reference only if some ## Lists bullet names its class, or some other rule lists it. Corpus: story:reference-names-the-public-surface owes a reference that names 'every element I made public and no element I kept internal'; concept:docspec says 'A docspec for reference documentation also names the classes of public surface the documentation must name in full' and 'the surface intent says which classes are public, and a reference docspec names the classes it must list'; decision:surface-members-listed-at-need says 'A builder who writes reference documentation lists the members of each class its docspec names as it writes'. The concept's 'classes of public surface ... name in full' reads most naturally as public-by-default classes listed whole, which option A strains: under A, ## Lists names an internal class and the reference lists only part of it, so the concept's sentence wants a delta to say a listed class may be internal and is listed for its public exceptions. Under B, nothing in the corpus says how the public exceptions of an internal class reach any reference, so the story's 'every element I made public' fails for them unless a new rule adds it. Harm at stake: a public element of an internal class missing from every reference (the story's promise); no accept-list entry is in play, this is a commitment choice. Options: A. ## Lists may name an internal class, listing only its public exceptions, as built; cost: a reader of ## Lists sees an internal class named, and concept:docspec takes a delta. B. ## Lists names only classes public by default, and a second rule makes every reference docspec list the public exceptions of internal classes; cost: a second listing rule, and a reference must decide which internal classes' exceptions are its own. C. ## Lists names only public-by-default classes, and an owner who makes an internal class's member public declares a public class for such members in the surface intent; cost: the surface intent grows a class per carve-out, and until the owner adds one the element reaches no reference with nothing noticing.
